worker_selection.rationale: Task 2 changes the accepted fail-closed Host boundary, maintained specs and D1Q-01 through D1Q-05.
The diff changes executable admission order, Host identity facts and a shared trust-boundary error type.
The focused suite is green while the full gate is red, and test doubles can hide production process ordering.
The new unavailable path, process-boundary projection and no-fallback recovery semantics are acceptance-critical.
Capability admission, driver selection, provenance and legacy N=1 compatibility cross module ownership boundaries.
Model-facing contract wording is fully covered by the independent spec lens; comments do not add a separate risk axis for this task.

findings.title: Effectful identity probes run before the fail-closed Host gate
findings.trigger: A caller invokes the ordinary ACP-first ZCode route without forcing the CLI transport.
findings.impact: Driver selection may execute the adapter and App runtime version probes before the retained qualification rejects the Packet, so unqualified Host-side code runs outside the claimed pre-launch effect boundary and D1-AC03/D1Q-01 are not satisfied.
findings.evidence: run calls chooseExecutionDriver at lines 905-910 and only calls enforcementAdmission at lines 943-950. The production selector executes every identity probe with spawnSync before returning, while the new prose at lines 937-942 and product.md lines 114-121 says no Host process exists before admission.
findings.suggestion: Make the unavailable qualification decision before any executable identity probe, or split driver selection into a pure transport choice followed by admission and then attestation. Keep the decision capability-driven and do not add a provider-brand branch.

findings.title: The required full release gate is red after the spec update
findings.trigger: The mandatory npm run verify:release gate validates the canonical research-distillate source bindings after the Task 2 product and architecture specs change.
findings.impact: The gate exits 1 because research-distillate.md still binds the dispatch-time Git blobs, so D1Q-05 and the task's definition of done are unmet even though the focused suite passes.
findings.evidence: The independent full run reported 708/710 with .ultra/specs/product.md actual blob d69182afca8e25e8213e9171b3fe23ac285e1e52 versus expected 776bdc8136d54825248573e52729678649fddd7c; architecture has the analogous stale row identified by the writer. research-distillate.md was frozen outside the initial twelve-path packet.
findings.suggestion: Record a Plan disposition that adds only .ultra/specs/research-distillate.md to the repair inventory, refresh its two exact source blob rows through the sole ZCode writer, and rerun the full release gate.

findings.title: The public process boundary does not return the promised typed diagnostic
findings.trigger: An installed Skill or the ubp delegate compatibility command hits host_enforcement_unavailable through its normal CLI process boundary.
findings.impact: Callers receive exit 1 plus human prose but no stable code or typed admission object, so an automated Supervisor cannot distinguish this safety gate from unrelated launch failures without parsing English text.
findings.evidence: HostEnforcementUnavailableError carries code and admission in memory, but main's catch writes only error.message. The test obtains the typed fields by requiring run inside a custom node -e wrapper rather than exercising either public CLI entry point.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the bounded human message but emit one stable machine-readable diagnostic carrying the error code and redacted admission at both direct Skill and ubp delegate process boundaries, then test those exact entry points.

findings.title: Admission is downstream of executable candidate inspection
findings.trigger: selectExecutionDriver evaluates an ACP candidate that declares identityProbes before the Packet's enforcement dimensions have been admitted.
findings.impact: The supposedly fail-closed path can execute unqualified adapter or runtime code with the probe environment before it rejects the Packet, leaving file and network effects outside the enforcement decision.
findings.evidence: The call at line 905 precedes the gate at line 943. selectExecutionDriver synchronously invokes identity probes for the selected profile before returning; the gate therefore cannot make the statement at lines 939-940 true.
findings.suggestion: Move a provider-neutral all-transports-unavailable precheck ahead of driver selection, or split pure selection from process-backed identity attestation and run attestation only after admission permits that candidate.

findings.title: Typed enforcement state is discarded by both CLI launchers
findings.trigger: HostEnforcementUnavailableError crosses the direct delegate.cjs or bin/install.js process boundary.
findings.impact: Automation loses error.code, admission dimensions and the evidence digest, collapsing a recoverable capability stop into an untyped generic process error.
findings.evidence: The error object defines code and admission, but delegate.cjs prints only message; bin/install.js awaits handle and its top-level catch likewise prints only Fatal plus message. No canonical JSON failure projection is emitted.
findings.suggestion: Centralize one redacted error projection for these two existing launchers and make the process output include the stable code, admission and recovery-safe message without exposing environment values.

findings.title: The installed diagnostic cites evidence that is not packaged
findings.trigger: A user invokes the installed npm package outside this development repository and receives the ZCode unavailable diagnostic.
findings.impact: The error cites .ultra/evidence/vnext-d1-host-enforcement-qualification/host-enforcement-receipt.json, but npm pack excludes the repository .ultra tree, so the stated recovery and audit reference does not exist in the installed product.
findings.evidence: package.json publishes the ultra-delegate Skill and selected docs but no repository .ultra/evidence path; npm pack --dry-run succeeds with 141 entries and contains no host-enforcement-receipt.json.
findings.suggestion: When an inspectable shipped receipt is needed, place the redacted immutable observation under the existing Skill reference tree and bind that packaged path, or explicitly distinguish a source-repository-only provenance URI from an installed recovery path.

findings.title: Admission compares retained identity with expected profile constants
findings.trigger: A later positive qualification record is evaluated after an adapter or runtime is rebuilt without changing its reported version markers.
findings.impact: identityMatch compares qualified_identity with profile.acp.candidateIdentity, which is another expected constant rather than the concrete observed candidate result, so a same-marker replacement can inherit a prior positive capability claim.
findings.evidence: The receipt retains adapter and runtime SHA-256 values, but the qualification record and identityMatch use only buildMarker/runtimeVersion fields. The current negative record remains unavailable, so this does not presently admit ZCode effects.
findings.suggestion: Do not promote a future supported record until admission consumes a concrete observed identity attestation appropriate to that Host; keep the current negative route simple rather than adding unused attestation machinery now.

findings.title: The no-launch tests bypass the production pre-admission probes
findings.trigger: A regression leaves chooseExecutionDriver and its identityProbes ahead of enforcementAdmission while the focused test suite runs.
findings.impact: All 192 focused tests pass even though the normal ACP-first route can execute adapter/runtime probe processes before the fail-closed gate.
findings.evidence: The shared start helper always sets ULTRA_DELEGATE_FORCE_CLI=1. The ACP refusal case injects chooseExecutionDriver as an already-computed object at lines 783-789, so neither branch observes whether the production selector ran a process before admission.
findings.suggestion: Add one deterministic regression using a fake executable identity probe that records invocation, then assert an all-transports-unavailable qualification rejects before that marker can be written. Keep provider access disabled.

findings.title: The typed-error test observes an internal wrapper instead of the public CLI
findings.trigger: The direct Skill entrypoint or ubp delegate drops the typed error fields while run still throws the rich Error object in process.
findings.impact: The test remains green and D1Q-01 appears satisfied although real automation receives only unstructured stderr.
findings.evidence: The fixture constructs node -e code that requires run, catches the Error itself, and manually JSON.stringify's code/name/admission. It never invokes delegate.cjs or bin/install.js as the caller would.
findings.suggestion: Exercise both public process entry points, require nonzero status plus one parseable bounded diagnostic with the stable code and redacted admission, and retain the existing no-artifact/no-fence assertions.

findings.title: Contract regexes accept an evidence path absent from the tarball
findings.trigger: The maintained docs and profile cite a repository-local qualification receipt while npm packaging excludes that file.
findings.impact: The contract suite passes because it matches the literal .ultra/evidence path, but an installed user cannot resolve the evidence the diagnostic names.
findings.evidence: Lines 1637 and 1644 assert only that the path text appears. npm pack --dry-run includes the Skill and docs but no host-enforcement-receipt.json.
findings.suggestion: If the evidence ref is intended to be installed, assert its referent appears in the packed file list and its digest matches; otherwise assert source-only provenance wording and avoid presenting it as an installed recovery path.

findings.title: The recoverable safety stop becomes an untyped generic CLI failure
findings.trigger: Host enforcement rejects a Packet and the Error leaves the JavaScript call stack through the documented command-line interface.
findings.impact: The next controller cannot select the unavailable-capability repair path from a stable code and may treat it like spawn, auth or malformed-input failure; machine recovery depends on parsing prose.
findings.evidence: HostEnforcementUnavailableError records code UBP_HOST_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE and structured admission, but the CLI catch emits only error.message. The compatibility launcher has the same loss at its top-level catch.
findings.suggestion: Project this known error into one bounded JSON failure shape at the existing process boundary and keep unknown exceptions generic; add public-entrypoint tests so code and admission cannot be dropped again.

findings.title: The refusal claims no Host process after process-backed probes may run
findings.trigger: ACP-first driver selection executes identity probes and then the enforcement decision rejects the selected route.
findings.impact: The source contract and resulting recovery narrative assert a stronger no-process boundary than the runtime provides, hiding the only pre-denial execution window from operators and reviewers.
findings.evidence: chooseExecutionDriver is called at line 905 before this block and its production identity inspection spawns commands. The comment at lines 939-940 says no Host process exists, while the error message describes a pre-launch refusal without disclosing those probes.
findings.suggestion: Prevent the probes before denial; if any non-provider preflight remains necessary, name it explicitly in the typed receipt rather than claiming zero Host-side process execution.

findings.title: Capability admission does not own the first executable boundary
findings.trigger: A Host profile combines executable candidate inspection with an enforcement record that should reject the Packet before Host-side code executes.
findings.impact: The driver layer performs process-backed discovery before the admission layer can enforce its invariant, so the supposedly central gate is bypassed by its own upstream dependency.
findings.evidence: The data flow is permission -> chooseExecutionDriver -> experimental disclosure -> enforcementAdmission -> fence. chooseExecutionDriver is not pure because identityProbes execute commands; therefore admission is not the first effect boundary.
findings.suggestion: Use the existing two concepts in the opposite order: make a pure capability/transport eligibility decision first, then run process-backed candidate attestation only for a route that could be admitted. Do not add a workflow engine or second Host registry.

findings.title: Installed policy is coupled to development-only qualification provenance
findings.trigger: The ultra-delegate Skill is installed from the npm package into another repository.
findings.impact: The runtime decision ships as constants while its named evidence remains only in this source checkout, so provenance ownership is ambiguous between product asset and project task evidence.
findings.evidence: HOST_ENFORCEMENT_QUALIFICATION embeds the local task attempt and receipt path. The package includes the Skill tree but excludes .ultra/evidence, and the record has no packaged immutable observation consumer.
findings.suggestion: Keep project task evidence as coordinator authority and, only if installed runtime diagnostics must cite it, ship one read-only redacted Skill-local evidence asset with the same digest. Avoid a database, registry or generated mirror.

findings.title: No-record Hosts are indistinguishable from positively admitted Hosts
findings.trigger: A later Step 1 controller calls enforcementAdmission for a Host whose legacy N=1 conformance passed but whose factory effect dimensions were never qualified.
findings.impact: The returned route is admitted with gate null and no explicit not-qualified state, so a new factory consumer could mistake legacy compatibility for D1 factory admission unless it adds another check.
findings.evidence: The no-record branch returns admitted and the unit test explicitly preserves that behavior for five Hosts. Current docs call it conformance-gated admission with no capability claim, and Step 1 is not yet implemented, so existing N=1 compatibility is not presently broken.
findings.suggestion: Before Step 1 consumes this API, expose the legacy/no-claim state distinctly or require the Supervisor Profile to demand an enforcement-qualified gate; do not globally disable existing N=1 delegation in this task.

positive_observations: The observed ZCode result is represented conservatively: unsupported and unobserved dimensions remain unavailable, transport authorization never becomes Worker effect authority, and experimental maturity is unchanged.
The implementation reuses the existing Host profile, permission, driver and result boundaries without adding a sandbox, daemon, database, retry loop or provider-brand semantic branch.
The twelve-path write scope and all fifty-five frozen outside-scope entries remained byte-identical to their admitted baselines.
limitations: All five selected lenses ran sequentially in one Codex context; this is the continuous Task Review, not the later Codex plus Claude stage Review.

The full gate also found a Task 1 Acceptance-section hash serialized with one extra newline. That file is outside this Task 2 packet and requires an explicit coordinator-owned reopen, fresh review and evidence publication rather than an in-place rewrite.

Current P2 findings remain non-blocking and are not auto-repaired: the unshipped evidence ref, future positive-record identity attestation, package-reference coverage, development-provenance coupling and explicit no-record factory state.
The three earlier D1 P2s remain retained: Host-created sessions outside portable observation, weaker non-Linux start identity, and stale fence-registry lock cleanup after a crash.
No commit, push, tag, publish, deploy, real-HOME install, credential operation, provider retry or production effect is covered by this Review.
